title: A History of Violence
full_review:
Full Review

If you thought by its poster that "Into the Blue" (MGM-Columbia) would be a good-looking but empty-headed underwater action movie, you'd be right!

Set in the Bahamas, the film stars Paul Walker as a diving instructor and Jessica Alba as his bikinied girlfriend, who both wind up in deep trouble when they discover a downed plane full of cocaine while searching for a storied shipwreck loaded with pirate treasure.

Despite its attractive cast and luscious Caribbean locales, director John Stockwell's flick is sunk by a flimsy plot and a B-movie script waterlogged with bad dialogue and gratuitous shots of the film's scantily clad leads.

The film has action violence, including shark-attack gore, some sexual situations and humor, suggested partial nudity, and recurring crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
